title: Usage trend forensics and SLA commitment handoff
summary: Quarterly check-in focusing on an anomalous usage spike in September, discussion of SLA commitment for upcoming pilot expansion, and alignment between engineering and finance on cost guardrails. Agreed to run a replay with canary workload, share granular cost model, and finalize a tied-down SLA with committed burst capacity by next week.
next_steps: Redwood: run peak-week replay on Dedicated pool and share perf/cost spreadsheet - due 2026-10-29
Vellum: share internal traffic pattern for promo week - due 2026-10-26
Samir: send draft SLA language and pricing addendum - due 2026-10-28
Kai: schedule follow-up alignment with finance and legal - due 2026-11-02
action_items: Samir - share perf/cost spreadsheet + replay notes - 2026-10-29
Jenna - set up replay with identical request mix and KV cache options - 2026-10-28
Maya - provide example payloads and percentiles for tail latency - 2026-10-26
Priya - confirm internal approval path for commitment and budget - 2026-10-30
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-23
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Kai (Redwood CSM), Maya (Vellum Head of ML), Liam (SRE), Priya (Finance), Arjun (Product)

Summary section (auto-gen may be rough):
- Short: Investigated Sept 12-14 spike; looks like combination of marketing-driven traffic + suboptimal batching on prefix cache misses. Finance concerned about unplanned overage. Customer wants SLA for pilot expansion and a clear rollback/fallback plan.

[00:00] Samir: okay we can get started, thanks everyone for joining, um I'll quickly run through the agenda, maya thanks for prepping the traffic extracts you sent, we'll go into the spike forensics then talk options for capacity commitment and SLA language, and end with next steps
[00:18] Maya: yep thanks Samir, quick note, we had a promo the week of sept 12, so a high qps window, but the cost was much higher than our estimate, and we're trying to understand why, not just the raw tokens but the perf tail
[00:30] Jenna: so I took your logs and the sampled traces, and there's two things that jumped out - one is batching dropped because many requests missed the prefix cache, and two there were a handful of long KV-cache deserialization events during cold starts
[00:50] Liam: yeah we saw autoscale spin up late, so the sustained tail was higher than expected, and that bumped us into on-demand capacity for a few hours
[01:05] Priya: and from finance perspective that map to a 42% overage for that billing period which is, uh, painful, we need predictability as we scale the pilot
[01:20] Samir: totally understood - to be clear there are levers: caching, batching windows, and reserved capacity (Dedicated) with a burst pool. We can model the unit economics two ways. I'll talk through the numbers I prepared — quick screen share of the perf/cost sheet (notes: link shared in chat: drive.redwood/vellum-replay)
[01:40] Speaker 6: got it, i see the doc, thanks
[02:10] Jenna: looking at the example traces, the average latency didn't change that much, but p95 and p99 moved a lot when cache misses hit. The root cause seems to be a sudden change in request prefix variety during the promo, which reduced cache hit ratios from ~68% to ~21% for that window
[02:40] Maya: prefix variety meaning customers were hitting new prompts? yes we had a campaign that altered the query structure, so that checks out
[02:55] Jenna: exact. And that interacts with batching heuristics in the runtime — if many unique prefixes are present, continuous batching efficiency drops and per-token cost increases because we lose batching benefits
[03:15] Samir: two immediate mitigation paths: one, improve prefix normalization on your side (we can share heuristics), and two, reserve Dedicated capacity with a small committed baseline and configured burst to absorb promotional spikes
[03:34] Arjun: question: is dedicated a hard isolation? we want to ensure no noisy neighbors cause tail latency issues
[03:42] Jenna: Dedicated gives you isolation of the GPU pool and predictable throughput; noisy neighbors are not a problem there. The tradeoff is cost commitment vs flexibility
[03:58] Liam: and how fast is burst capacity? if demand triples in 30 minutes from a campaign, will it come up in time or will we see the same tail spikes?
[04:15] Jenna: autoscale is configurable, you can set aggressive scale policies, but it still takes time to provision more nodes. The burst pool is pre-warmed capacity that we can keep available for you in Dedicated — that comes with a fixed monthly fee for reservation plus burst usage pricing
[04:36] Priya: so we need modeling: what would a realistic commit look like for our traffic? we prefer a blended cost view across likely, worst-case, and ideal windows
[04:52] Samir: absolutely. I prepared three scenarios in the spreadsheet: baseline (current), promo-adjusted (50% increase in unique prefixes), and worst-case (100% increase). For each we compute committed cost, expected overage, and a blended per-token unit. The promo-adjusted scenario shows Dedicated with 20% lower blended cost vs hosted if you commit to 60% of peak sustained throughput
[05:20] Maya: hmm 60% of peak sustained — what about the dev/test environments? we don't want to pay for unused capacity by devs}
[05:31] Samir: you can have separate small development pools on hosted and route production to Dedicated. Also we offer automatic fallback: if Dedicated is saturated, traffic will failover to hosted model variants (cheaper/less powerful) rather than dropping requests, or you can set queueing policies
[05:52] Liam: is there a throttle or circuit breaker for costs? we want a hard stop if projected spend crosses a threshold before finance signs off
[06:05] Kai: yes we can configure spend guardrails with alerts and hard limits; hard limits will start rejecting traffic, soft limits will route to cheaper variants. We can also export daily burn reports to your finance S3 bucket or via our Console API
[06:24] Priya: daily burn reports are good, but we need an approval flow: alert finance + AE for >10% daily delta vs forecast
[06:33] Samir: noted, we'll include that in the ops runbook we hand off
[06:40] [08:00] Speaker 1 (mis-labeled): there was also a chunk of traffic coming from a third-party integration that retried aggressively which multiplied the effective qps during the promo, that was noisy
[08:20] Maya: yes that third-party partner had a bug, we rolled a fix midday but the retries were already queued and caused additional cache churn
[08:34] Jenna: that also affects prefix diversity, because retried requests had altered metadata and resulted in different prompt preambles so caches couldn't help
[08:45] Samir: ok so technical fixes on your side (partner retry logic + prefix normalization) plus a Dedicated baseline for predictability, plus canary replays to validate — three-pronged approach
[09:05] Arjun: on the SLA language, we want guaranteed throughput and latency targets for production peak windows, and financial credits for breaches. what's typical?
[09:20] Samir: our standard Dedicated SLA for enterprise pilots guarantees 99.9% uptime for the endpoint and p95 latency targets depending on model profile; we can attach credits for missed SLOs in the addendum — the normal cadence is 10% credit tiered to severity, but we can draft custom tiers for your pilot
[09:42] Priya: we will need precise definitions in the SLA: how do you define 'sustained peak window' and how is burst priced? Also what telemetry do you expose so we can audit compliance?
[09:58] Jenna: we expose per-route token breakdowns, tail latency histograms, and node-level traces in the Console. For audit we provide daily logs, retention options, and we can do a joint runbook review monthly. Burst is priced at a higher per-token rate but with a clear cap
[10:20] Maya: can we get a sample SLA with definitions? even a redline to start with legal
[10:28] Samir: yes I'll send a draft SLA redline by 2026-10-28. I'll include the telemetry endpoints and the reporting cadence.
[10:39] [12:10] Priya: from a finance POV, the key ask is a modeling spreadsheet with sensitivity knobs: prefix diversity, percent cache hit, average token length, and percent of traffic on Dedicated vs hosted. we want to present that to execs next week
[12:32] Samir: that's the sheet I shared, but I'll add interactive knobs and a promo-sensitivity tab
[12:40] Jenna: also worth mentioning quantization profiles if you want to shift to a cheaper model variant for non-critical requests; that can cut per-token cost by 20-40% while keeping nominal quality for certain endpoints
[13:00] Maya: we do have endpoints that are non-customer-facing that could tolerate a lower-quality model, yes
[13:10] Samir: ok we'll map endpoints into quality tiers and show savings in the model
[13:25] [15:20] Liam: security question — if we go Dedicated in our VPC setup (private), how's key management handled? do you manage KMS or do we bring our own?
[15:32] Jenna: for Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for Dedicated in our hosted control plane we offer KMS integration with customer keys via KMS passthrough. We also provide audit logs and SOC2 artifacts on request
[15:50] Maya: we will likely require customer-managed KMS once we move sensitive data sets; is there an impact on latency for KMS operations?
[15:58] Jenna: KMS calls are out-of-band for model storage keys; runtime doesn't call KMS per-request. So negligible latency impact on inference. It only affects key rotation and model load/unload ops
[16:12] Priya: legal will want the SOC2 report and encryption detail; can you share those docs?
[16:19] Samir: yes, I'll attach SOC2 type II and an architecture note for KMS/HSM.
[16:25] [18:00] Maya: re: the replay test you mentioned, what fidelity will it have? we need to ensure it's representative: same QPS distribution, same prefix variety, payload sizes, and retry behavior
[18:13] Jenna: we'll run a replay harness that consumes your anonymized traffic trace. We can toggle KV cache warmed vs cold, run with your exact batching heuristics, and report p50/p95/p99 and token counts. We'll also run a variant that uses the Dedicated pool with burst pre-warmed to show the delta
[18:37] Samir: estimated time to set up replay is 48-72 hours once we have the traffic sample. Jenna will coordinate.
[18:45] Maya: we'll upload the trace to the secure bucket by monday
[18:49] Samir: perfect
[19:05] [22:00] Priya: one more ask: can you show us a forecast of monthly burn for next 6 months for three adoption scenarios? execs want projection for budget planning
[22:15] Samir: yes, the spreadsheet will include a 6-month forecast and Monte Carlo banding for promo events. We'll include a conservative run with a 95th percentile scenario
[22:30] Arjun: technical deep-dive request: after the replay, can we do a follow-up run with KV cache tuning and different batching window lengths to validate improvements?
[22:45] Jenna: absolutely; we'll document the exact config and results so you can adopt the tuning in production
[23:00] Speaker 6: can we also see the tracing hooks you'd need to integrate with our APM?
[23:12] Jenna: yes we have tracing connectors for NewRelic and Datadog, and you can also ingest our trace samples into your APM via our events API
[23:25] [30:00] Maya: any competitive intel — our legal asked if Redwood has agreements with cloud providers or if there's any vendor lock-in we should be aware of
[30:12] Samir: we run on multiple clouds and we offer exportable model artifacts and data exports — no lock-in; we also provide an on-prem private deployment option if required. Competitors you mentioned (anthropic/opencloud) have different tradeoffs, but our differentiation is tooling for production economics and the observability into token-level cost
[30:38] Priya: thanks, that's good to know
[31:00] [36:00] Samir: ok recap — agreed approach: 1) Vellum uploads anonymized promo traffic by monday (2026-10-26) 2) Redwood runs replay: cold and warmed cache, hosted vs Dedicated (target deliverable 2026-10-29) 3) Samir to share SLA redline + pricing scenarios (2026-10-28) 4) Finance to review forecast (Priya) and confirm budget by 2026-10-30 5) Follow-up meeting to review replay results and SLA redline scheduled for 2026-11-02 at 10am PT
[36:35] Maya: sounds good, one more small ask — can you include a short one-page summary of recommended ops runbook items for promos (pre-warm cache, partner backoff, throttle policy)?
[36:50] Kai: yes we'll include an ops checklist and a recommended throttle policy. We'll also include a suggested rollout for canary traffic and guardrails
[37:05] Priya: ok thanks everyone, this helps. We'll prioritize legal/finance review next week
[37:16] Samir: great, thanks all. Jenna, any final notes from your end?
[37:22] Jenna: nothing more, I'll start the replay setup once we have the trace and I'll ping the team in the shared doc
[37:30] [52:11] Meeting ended
